purpose: Bromfenac is an eye drop used to reduce pain and swelling in your eye after cataract surgery. It helps your eye heal more comfortably by controlling inflammation. Your doctor prescribes it to keep your eye from feeling sore, red, or irritated after the procedure.
how_it_works: Bromfenac works by blocking certain chemicals in your body called prostaglandins, which cause pain and swelling. Think of it like putting a tiny anti-inflammatory directly into your eye. By stopping those chemicals, it helps calm down the irritation and discomfort after surgery.
common_side_effects: Some people may notice mild burning, stinging, or itching right after putting in the drops. Your eye might look a little red or feel slightly irritated. These feelings usually go away quickly and are not dangerous.
warnings: Do not wear soft contact lenses while using these drops unless your doctor says it is okay. Tell your doctor if you are allergic to aspirin or other NSAIDs like ibuprofen, since you could also be allergic to bromfenac. Using it longer than recommended or too frequently can actually slow healing, so always follow your doctor's instructions carefully. Stop using it and call your doctor if your vision changes or your eye pain gets worse.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one drop into the affected eye once a day, starting one day before cataract surgery and continuing for about two weeks afterward. Always follow your eye doctor's specific instructions, as they may adjust this schedule for you.
